howToUse: 1. Copy one entry's `prompt` field verbatim into fal.ai (nano banana / Gemini 2.5 Flash Image).
2. Save the returned image, then tell Claude which `id` it corresponds to and where the file was saved.

3. Claude will inspect the image with vision to confirm every letter actually printed on the image matches an item in that entry's `expectedLabels` (for hotspot entries only — the 3 picture-composition entries at the end have no letters to check, only scene fidelity), note (and skip, not guess) any duplicated/ambiguous printed letters, run `npm run images:webp` (from web/) to convert the source PNG to WebP in place, add/reuse an entry in the shared cross-skill registry `web/src/lib/photoImages.ts` (never inline the image/part data directly in a skill file), wire a multi-Bloom's-tier set of question branches into the skill file(s) named in `targetSkillFile` per RIGOR-STANDARDS.md, and verify (tsc + lint + a real request against the running dev server) before calling it done.

4. If any part is missing an arrow/letter, or a letter's arrow lands on the wrong structure, regenerate with a corrected prompt (add an explicit correction line naming the missing/misplaced part) rather than accepting a partial image — every part in `expectedLabels` must be identifiable.

5. An image is not tied to the one skill in `targetSkillFile` — once registered in photoImages.ts, reuse it from any other skill (same or different subject, same grade) that has a genuine curriculum reason to reference it, per curriculum-reference/CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md's photo-diagram section.

6. For the 3 picture-composition entries (g8-eng-market-honesty-scene, g8-eng-radio-arrival-scene, g8-ksw-mighani-hero-scene): do NOT wire these as hotspot questions. Their `integrationPlan` field instead describes a new comprehension/description question branch — a 'describe what is happening in this picture' or 'answer these questions about the scene' style prompt — since there are no lettered parts to identify.
_meta.styleGuideSummary: All prompts embed the same style block so every generated image reads as one consistent visual system across the whole app — do not vary the style between images. Object/material galleries use a soft 3D-rendered matte style with studio lighting and a muted pastel palette; maps and landscape/vegetation scenes use a clean flat-vector illustration style with soft natural colours; the 3 narrative picture-composition scenes use a warm, richly-coloured flat-illustration storybook style (generic, non-identifiable figures, never photorealistic real people) since they are meant to prompt writing/description rather than hotspot identification.
_meta.criticalRule: For every hotspot-style image (all entries except the 3 picture-composition ones at the end): the prompt instructs nano banana NOT to print any part's name as text anywhere on the image — only a circled bold capital letter + thin leader line per part. This is deliberate and different from typical stock 'labeled diagram' images (which usually print full text labels): text labels would give the answer away before the question is even asked. If a returned image has any part's name printed as text, it must be regenerated. For the 3 picture-composition entries, the rule is the opposite and equally strict: NO letters, NO leader lines, NO text of any kind anywhere on the image — it must be a single clean, unlabelled illustrative scene, since its whole purpose is to be described by the learner, not have its parts pointed out to them.
_meta.displayConstraint: Confirmed in web/src/components/visuals/Visual.tsx's PhotoDiagram renderer: images display at max-height 420px, max-width 672px (Tailwind max-w-2xl), object-contain, width 100% of container. Source images at roughly 1024-1200px on the long edge are plenty — this is never a print asset. The `dimensions` field on each entry below states the generation aspect ratio/size that best fits that constraint.
